reading:
Figure Ground has been the tour's most consistent winner: #1 in heat b in both rounds (Lit Manual 8.02, then Lit Manual, Railed 8.01, with 7 top fours and 7 promise votes). Every time it won, it was for one thing. A fix became a rule you can see on the page: "a figure touches its rows." Every list in time is a rail. Each stop sits level with its row, the dates sit in a timetable margin, and a lit NOW line leaves the rail and crosses the list. Six lenses called To do's NOW line, splitting late from coming, the best device in the heat. Type loved the named type tokens on a 4px grid, the space-padded tabular rail dates, the 'Fig.' captions and "Tell Vera what to plan." Interaction and usability loved the sight line (title, box, Send, with the tube on the right), the textarea as the first Tab stop and the phone's jump keys.

What held Railed back, most-cited first:
1. The chat's ~950px dotted leaders. All eight lenses named them. They ruled the thread like notebook paper; the crit's literal "leader to the speaker" did that.
2. Status lit 'This page' green while Settings says Sign-in needs a look: a lamp that lies (system, interaction, usability, skeptic).
3. The blueprint grid sheets read as navy slabs at a squint (feedback, soul, skeptic).
4. Soul sat at 7.5 because the monitors were unchanged. The owner wants the tube's light back: the relit treatment from Relit, the Plans countdown or round tube from Gauged, the spend tube up in the first screen, and the full E1 halo on 'plan'.
5. Smaller faults:
   - Home has two NOW lines at different heights, and its plate lights three marks.
   - Next up is said twice (in the tube and in row 1).
   - The Plans month's week ranges sit 18px off their stops, and the empty weeks are not folded.
   - Restaurant shares amber with late.
   - To do's Show is a select plus a Filter press.
   - '2 late' and 'All 4' are two links to one page.
   - Home's '#n' ids and 12-13px eyebrows.
   - There is no 22px step between Home's 52px question and its 28px plate heads.

The lineage's grafts lost both times (7.3, 7.2) when they laid notation over rows (hatching, dimension lines) or put instruments in place of drawings. They scored when they drew data and replaced something (the round Plans tube, the folded weeks).

To win round 3, the refine has to land every named fix and visibly relight the tubes (soul is the weak lens), with Home's first screen changing: one NOW, a countdown tube, the 22px plate step. The graft has to bring a new drawing that only this lineage would make. The lineage's own brief always promised "Home's family tree to Vera to its counts" and never built it. That figure can replace the duplicate Next up, and it must keep the rail rule intact.

Titles: "Tell Vera what to plan." was best or joint best in all eight heat-b notes and stays on the refine. The graft tries an untried variant that answers the skeptic's "presumes a plan" and fits a figure wiring the family to her.

briefs.name: Lit Manual, Relit Rails
briefs.hypothesis: Railed won on one rule that holds everywhere, a figure touches its rows. It lost points only on named, fixable faults: the ruled chat, the green lamp that lies, navy sheets, unlit tubes, and two NOW lines on Home. Fixing all of them and switching the tubes back on in the manual's own terms should lift soul (its weakest lens, 7.5) without costing type, interaction or usability (8.3-8.6). Applying the rule literally to the chat (each arrow drawn in its own message's row) also ends the lineage's oldest open fault. Home's first screen changes visibly: a countdown tube, one NOW line, a 22px plate step and sky time ink. The lesson that a refinement must move Home's first screen is met.
briefs.brief:
Start from t2-figure-refine (palettes/t2-figure-refine.json, variants/t2-figure-refine/sheet.css and templates/). Keep the plate grammar: a fixed figure column (--fig-w 16.5rem) behind one vertical hairline on every page, login and 404 included. Keep the rails with stops level with their rows, the lit NOW line that leaves the rail and crosses the list, the 'Fig. N' caption (bold blueprint number, then one sentence saying how to read it), bone ink on green-black, the steel 'here', and the named type tokens. TOKENS (sheet.css :root and palette): - The sheet. --sheet #0f161c becomes #0e1513, a green-black only a step off --bg. --sheet-edge #26313a becomes #24302c. --grid-bold falls from 0.12 to 0.06 alpha, and --grid-fine from 0.07 to 0.03. The fine grid goes from 12px to 24px (background-size 48px 48px, 24px 24px). Blue lives only in the lines (--draw, --draw-2); the sheet stops reading as a navy slab. - Add --when: #aebccb, one low-chroma sky ink for time. Rail dates take it on every rail (the weekday in --dim, the day and month in --when). It is the one grounded companion the content rows lacked (style). - Add --clay: #c79071 for the Restaurant and Something to eat kind squares. #f1af64 (people) is spent only on late and needs-a-look. - Add --t-plate: 600 1.375rem/28px var(--f-display) for Home's plate heads (Coming up, To do, Finish setting up, The kids' wishes, Lately added). Home's ranks then read 52 question > 22 plate > 16 row. Inner pages keep --t-head (28px) under their 48px titles. - Eyebrows and legends ('Who answers', 'What a lamp says', 'Show one kind', the tally key, the 'Week' column head) are 14px sentence case: 600 0.875rem/20px var(--f-text), no tracking, never mono caps. Drawing words stay mono and rise to 13px minimum. PHOSPHOR (phosphor_kit.md). The light goes back where the phosphor is, and stays off everywhere else: - E1 in full on 'plan': text-shadow 0 0 .45em rgb(109 255 156/.45), 0 0 1.3em rgb(109 255 156/.22). The question itself stays bone. - The NOW line on every rail: 2px #6dff9c with two layers (box-shadow 0 0 4px rgb(109 255 156/.7), 0 0 14px rgb(109 255 156/.3)). Its node is a lamp with a #e4fff0 core in a phosphor halo (E20, breathing 4s). The NOW word is 14px sentence case 'Now' in --brand with E1, not 10px caps. - Every monitor (Home's Next up, the Plans tube, the Status spend tube, the Ideas radar, the Settings machine's screen, 404 and login) gets the full E12-E17 treatment: - VT323 at three strengths (dim at 55%, normal, bright with the E13 three-halo bloom); - a 0.35px blur on the glass text; - E14 1-in-3 scanlines, a top-left sheen and corners falling into shadow (radial-gradient to #000 at 70%); - the case's breathing power lamp; - E16 power-on with the warm-up cut to 0.1s, never over the glass that holds the question. - Any live mark smaller than 1.2rem in a drawing is an E20 lamp (glowing dot), never a small tube: To do's next-due mark, the newest chat arrow's head, the wiring's live port. - The greeting's E7 pool stays under Send only; no haze over the plates below. - The row afterglow. Pointing at a rail row lights its stop at once (0.12s) and fades over 1.2s (--afterglow), with a 2px phosphor left edge on the row fading on the same curve (the lesson: the edge must be phosphor green, not sage or steel). Nothing else glows on hover. HOME: - The greeting. The title stays first at left:

. Then the box, then Send. The tube stays at right. - The tube becomes the countdown, so Next up is said once: - the radar with only the next plan's blip lit and the rest matte at the dim strength (no tiny numerals); - 'Next in 1 day' in VT323 bright at 2rem; - '10:00 tomorrow' at normal strength; - '4 more on the rail ↓' at dim strength, a link to #coming. The plan's name is said by the rail's lit row 1. Below 48rem, where the rail is below the first screen, the tube also prints the name (.tube-name, display:none from 48rem), so the phone's first screen still says what is next. - Coming up: - Start the rail level with the plate head: move the 'Fig. 1' caption under the rail and drop the ~50px of empty figure column above the first stop. - Light one mark per figure: the NOW line and stop 1 at full light, the trace between them at half strength (stroke rgb(109 255 156/.45), no filter). - Rows keep the tabular mono time and the relative words. The dotted leader stops at the words cell, as now. - To do on Home. No second crossing NOW at another height: here NOW is a short lit tick on a 2px rail down the list's left edge, between the late rows and the rest ('Now' in 14px brand, an 18px lit tick, nothing crossing). The To do page keeps the full crossing line. - One way on in the head: 'All 4 · 2 late →', with '2 late' in amber, linking to /tasks#now. It replaces the separate '2 late' and 'All 4' links. #now on the To do page flashes on arrival (E10: ring and bloom fading over 1.2s; scroll-margin-top: calc(var(--bar-h) + 1rem)). - Finish setting up keeps its ringed track, with rows trimmed to 44px and 'Then you’re ready.' kept as plain text. Lately added drops the '#1'-'#4' ids. Its kind squares are 10px, and the kind word is 14px sentence case in ink-2. - Phone: keep the '4 more plans / 4 to do / 2 late' keys at 44px. CHAT. The sequence diagram is drawn in each message's own row, so nothing crosses the reading measure: - .seq-thread > li becomes a grid: grid-template-columns: var(--fig-w) 1fr. - The left cell (.seq-cell) carries the lanes as a repeating background: one 1px --draw line per lane at fixed x, on the --sheet ground with the faint grid, continuous down the thread. - Each row's cell draws its own arrow at that row's speaker line (--ay), from the speaker's lane to the lane it answers, numbered over it at 13px mono. - The arrow is an to its message. Pointing at a message lights its arrow. The newest arrow is the live mark: phosphor with E1 and an E20 head, and an E10 flash on arrival. - A 16px stub carries the arrow to the column's hairline and stops there. No leader enters the thread. - The lane heads (her glyph screen with bloom and scanlines, and the family's initials) sit sticky at the top of the figure column. - The date rule becomes a rail date in mono --when ('Sun 27 Sep'): a tick across the lanes and a hairline across the thread. - Vera's lines stay left on the black. The family's slips stay right in --slip with their steel edge. PLANS: - The head gets Gauged Manual's round tube (T2-42, from tour/t2-b/variants/t2-figure-graft), relit: E13 glass glow at the middle, three halos, 0.35px blur. It reads 'Next in 1 day' (VT323 bright, 1.5rem+) over 'then 1 more this week' (normal, 20px), and the lit arc of a ring marks the days to the next plan. It holds no name, so the list's lit row 1 says it once. List and Month share it. - The list. A rail with stops level with the rows and the NOW line crossing above row 1. Each row's grid and hairline stop at 46rem with its facts (max-width on .plan-rows). - The month: - Each week's range is centred on its stop: the stop at the row's vertical middle and the range beside it (align-items:center), never 18px under it. - Past weeks with nothing on fold behind a break mark: two 45-degree ticks across the rail, then one 32px strip, '31 Aug – 20 Sep · Nothing on', so the height goes to the weeks to come. - The NOW line runs from the rail into today's cell, whose outline is lit. - A filled stop means a week with plans. TO DO: - 'Show' becomes four latched 44px keys in one segmented row: Open, Late, Done, All. Each is a GET link that acts in one press, the current one in steel 'here' with its 2px cap. Search keeps its own field and button. - The list keeps the crossing NOW line (the signature). - The due column is a fixed 15rem, so 'Edit' always sits on the due line, never wrapping. - The '#4' follows the title at label size in --dim. - Late rows keep their 3px amber edge and the words 'Late · was due 3 days ago'. The checkbox frame stays neutral. - Fig. 1 tally: the next-due mark is an E20 lamp on its bar, not an outlined box. The legend is 14px sentence case: 'Late', 'Due', 'No date', 'Next due'. STATUS: - The head readings are '3 of 4 answering' and '1 of 4 key set' as links. The third reading is replaced by a round spend tube at the head's right: 168px, the same component as Plans, '$0.00' in VT323 bright at 2.25rem, 'of $2.00 today' at 20px, and the share as a lit arc. $ is stated once, in the first screen. - Under the head, one caution line with a 3px amber left edge on slate: 'Sign-in still uses the installer’s password. Choose your own password →'. - 'This page' is amber, both in the Connected list and on the wiring figure's port (amber ring, no green). - Every lamp carries its word beside it: 'Working', 'Off', 'Needs a look'. - The wiring's model is a lamp and the words 'gpt-6-luna' in --brand. Its ports are links to their rows (#c-weather and so on), with E10 on landing. - The lamp legend moves under the wiring at 14px. IDEAS: - Nearest and Furthest drop their '#7'/'#4' ids. - The kinds figure stays the Kind filter. On the phone, Kind keys return to the filter row. - The table splits drive time (right-aligned, tabular) from the compass in its own column. - The '#n' column stays at label size in --dim. - The radar tube gets the full relit treatment. SETTINGS: - The machine's screen gets E13/E14 (scanlines, blur, bloom). - The callout rings on the rows stay, with ring 8 amber. Each figure callout is a link to its row, landing with E10. - The figure column is sticky, so no dark band opens under it. - Section pages keep the anatomy figure with its live field lamp. FORM (idea_form): the anatomy figure's live mark is the field being typed in, as a lit outline with E20, alongside the E4 box glow on the real field. Labels are 14px. 'Add it' is the one primary, with the E3 ring and pool. SIGN-IN: the field sits in the main column beside the figure column (left edge at the hairline + 2rem), not hard left. Keep all controls 44px with sentence-case words, no ISO dates anywhere, underlined prose links in --link, and links in heads as bone on a 1px blueprint underline. Update docs/STYLE.md notes in the variant's comments only where the sheet changes a rule.
briefs.avoids: The 950px ruled chat. The green 'This page' lamp. Navy grid slabs. Unlit or dim monitors, and small VT323 'tubes' under 1.2rem. Two NOW lines at different heights on Home, and three lit marks in one plate. Next up said twice. The week range 18px off its stop. Empty past weeks taking the month's height. Amber on a kind. A select plus a Filter press. Two links to one page in one head. '#n' ids before or beside Home's titles. 12-13px mono eyebrows. A missing step between the question and the plate heads. Edit wrapping under the due words. Sign-in hard left. It adds no dimension lines, hatching or footer key (the pasted grafts of round 2), and no green beyond the short list.
briefs.title: "Tell Vera what to *plan*." Kept: the best title this lineage, or any heat-b design, has found, best or joint best in all eight round-2 notes. It names who hears you, says the whole job in one verb (weekends, ideas, reminders and the calendar are all things to plan), and reads as the manual's own imperative. The lit word lands at the line's end, where the eye stops. Set in bone with only 'plan' lit, it shows the E1 two-layer halo most clearly. It stays the box's <label>, holds one line on a phone at 2.25rem, and no other glow on Home claims 'plan': the tube now says 'Next in 1 day', not a plan's name.

briefs.name: Wired Household
briefs.hypothesis: The lineage's own brief always promised "Home's family tree to Vera to its counts" and never drew it. Home's tube still repeats the plan the rail's row 1 already names. The graft replaces that duplicate with Fig. 0, the household wired to Vera, drawn in phosphor on her glass. It is drawn from data the page holds: who is in the family, who spoke last and when, and what she keeps. Each terminal is a 44px way down the page, landing with a glow. So the greeting's green screen becomes this lineage's own figure: data, light and a link. That is what grafts took on (draw data the page holds and replace something), and it is not a Next up tube every lineage shares. Folding setup into one caution line and sending each figure mark to its row keep Home short and make the manual's figures an index. The rail rule stays untouched below, so the idea is still recognisable at a glance.
briefs.brief:
Start from t2-figure-refine (palettes/t2-figure-refine.json, variants/t2-figure-refine/), with its plate grammar, rails, crossing NOW line, captions and type tokens kept. Apply the lineage's most important fixes first:
- Chat leaders end at the figure column's hairline (a 16px stub). Each arrow is drawn level with its own message, in a per-row lane cell, and is a link to it.
- Status: 'This page' gets an amber lamp and port, every lamp has a word ('Working / Off / Needs a look'), and the spend becomes a round tube in the head ('$0.00 / of $2.00 today', VT323 20px+), so $ is said once.
- The sheet goes to green-black: --sheet #0e1513, grid alpha halved, 24px fine grid.
- E1 in full on the lit word.
- Restaurant and Something to eat go to --clay #c79071; amber is for late only.
- Plans takes Gauged's round 'Next in 1 day' tube (relit), with past empty weeks folded behind a break mark and week ranges centred on their stops.
- Lamps under 1.2rem are E20 dots.
Then graft four features, each rebuilt in the manual's ink, line and phosphor.

1. Fig. 0, 'The household' (L076, GEM), on Home's greeting, replacing the Next up radar tube.
The tube's case keeps its full E12-E17 light: VT323 three strengths, 0.35px blur, scanlines, sheen, corner falloff, the breathing power lamp, E16 at 0.1s and never over the question. About 26rem by 17rem at the greeting's right; the title, box and Send stay first at left. On the glass, drawn in an inline SVG in phosphor:
- At left, a column of the family's monograms (feature 2), one per member from the family list, each on a node.
- In the middle, her glyph screen (E19), about 7rem square, blooming.
- Wires from every member's node to her screen, matte at the dim strength (rgb(109 255 156/.35), 1.25px). The wire from whoever spoke last runs bright (#6dff9c, a 2px stroke under a blurred copy for the halo, since Chrome draws no shadow on SVG strokes).
- That member's node carries VT323 'Alex 19:52' at normal strength (20px), and the node is a link to /chat#newest. It is the 'Continue with Vera' way, drawn.
- At right, wires out of her screen to four terminals. Each is a real 44px <a> laid over the glass in VT323 at 1.25rem, normal strength:
  - '5 plans · next tomorrow' → #coming
  - '4 to do · 2 late' → #todo, with '2 late' in inverse video (late on glass is inverse, never amber phosphor)
  - '12 ideas' → #lately
  - 'Wishes' → #wishes
- Caption under the case: 'Fig. 0 Who talks to Vera, and what she keeps: the lit wire is whoever spoke last.'
- The plate heads below drop their counts, since the terminals say each count once. Coming up's head keeps 'Next up, then 4 more' only as words. The rail's lit stop 1 names the next plan, so nothing is said twice.
- With no family yet, the figure shows her screen and the four terminals only.
- Phone: the case stacks under the box at full width. Monograms run in a row above her screen, and the terminals become the existing 44px jump keys under the case ('5 plans · next tomorrow', '4 to do', '2 late', '12 ideas').
- Source: rounds/r12/variants/r12-mut-3/templates/chat.html (~21-45, speakers gathered from the lines; svg .her-case .her .wire .node .node-them .who-n) and rounds/r12/variants/r12-mut-3/sheet.css (~879-889, .tile-loop, sticky svg).
- Also on Chat, where it began: the lane heads of the row-keyed sequence diagram are the same roster wired to her screen, sticky at the top of the figure column, with the last speaker's wire lit.

2. People as monogram initials, no tiles (L088, GEM).
- Every person drawn on the page is their initial set large in Plex Sans Condensed 300 (not Fraunces), with no tile, ring or fill.
- Where it appears:
  - Fig. 0 (2rem);
  - Chat's lane heads, in place of the boxed 'S'/'A' tiles (2rem), and beside each family slip's time (1.25rem);
  - the To do tally's owner columns (1.5rem; Household keeps the lucide house icon at the same size);
  - the Family page roster (3rem beside each name).
- Grown-ups in bone (--heading). Kids in a low-chroma heather, --kid: #b9a8cc, never pink and never amber.
- Never larger than the words it marks: aria-hidden, with the name in text beside it.
- Source: rounds/r13/variants/r13-wmut-1/sheet.css (.initial and .roster 1234-1244, .said-them .avatar 1649, .kids-cell .initial 1676, .person-cell .avatar 2135); templates/chat.html and family.html there.

3. Glow where you land from a link (L112, GEM), the rule that makes every figure an index.
- Every mark in a figure that names a row is an <a> to that row:
  - Fig. 0's terminals;
  - the chat arrows (→ #m{{ id }});
  - the Status wiring's ports (→ their rows);
  - the Settings machine's numbered callouts (→ #part-N);
  - the rail stops on Home and Plans (→ their rows);
  - To do's tally cells (→ the task).
- The element landed on (:target) flashes a 1px #6dff9c ring and a 40px bloom (box-shadow 0 0 0 1px rgb(109 255 156/.7), 0 0 40px -6px rgb(109 255 156/.45)), fading over 1.8s on cubic-bezier(0.2,0.7,0.3,1).
- To do's #now re-strikes the NOW line: its halo starts at three times its width and settles.
- scroll-margin-top: calc(var(--bar-h) + 1rem). Off under prefers-reduced-motion, where the ring simply holds for the visit.
- One target at a time.
- Source: rounds/r11/variants/r11-wild-4/sheet.css (.frame:target {animation: landed 1.8s …} line 1076; @keyframes landed 1835-1837; reduced-motion 1840-1841).

4. Setup cut to one line (L042, GEM), rebuilt as the manual's Caution note.
- Home's 'Finish setting up' plate (about 245px) becomes one ruled plate of about 64px, directly under the greeting and above Coming up.
- In the figure column, hung the way a manual hangs its warnings: the lucide triangle-alert icon in a 2px amber ring at 2rem, and 'Caution' in 14px 600 amber sentence case beside it.
- In the words column, on slate with no amber fill: '**Choose your own password**, so everybody signs in as themselves. Then Telegram, then Google Calendar.' The first action is the link; the others are plain.
- At the right, 'All 3 steps →' (44px) to /setup.
- On the phone it wraps to two lines, each 'then X' held together (white-space: nowrap on each).
- The kids' wishes plate moves up beside Lately added.
- Source: rounds/r12/variants/r12-wild-4/sheet.css ~1118-1137 (.alert, .alert .legend, .alert-figure, .alert-one, .alert .rest) and templates/home.html there. Take only the one-line shape and its next-step link: the amber stays in the ring and word, with no amber gradient and no tracked legend.

The rest of Home:
- The Coming up rail starts level with its head. NOW and stop 1 are at full light, the trace between them at half.
- To do on Home uses a short lit 'Now' tick on its own 2px left rail, so only one NOW line crosses on Home.
- Plate heads use a 22px step (600 1.375rem/28px display).
- Rail dates are in a muted sky ink, --when #aebccb.
- Lately added drops its '#n' ids.

The other pages:
- Status, Settings, Ideas, To do, Plans and the form keep the parent's figures with the fixes above. The figure-marks-as-links rule (3) runs on all of them, and the monograms (2) appear wherever a person is drawn.
- To do's Show becomes segmented one-press keys (Open, Late, Done, All), with Edit on a fixed-width due line.

Keep 44px targets, sentence-case controls, no ISO dates, underlined prose links, and the textarea as the first Tab stop after the nav. Fig. 0's links come after Send in Tab order: the figure's markup follows the form, placed right by CSS grid.
briefs.avoids: Next up said twice, because the household figure takes the tube's place and the rail names the plan. The glass is still a real green screen, so the soul score is not lost. Two links to one page: each count is said once, at its terminal, and the plate heads drop theirs. A tall setup plate on Home. Figures that are only pictures: every mark is now a way to its row. Boxed letter tiles for people. Like the refine, it avoids the ruled chat, the lying lamp, navy slabs, amber kinds, small VT323 tubes and two NOW lines on Home. It does not take Master Caution's full-width amber band (the caution stays a hung manual note on slate), nor the switchboard's day-numeral lit pair, so heat b's lineages do not converge. It takes none of the main line's structures (no terminal column beside a desk, no listing bands, no matte plate, no big quote), and none of round 2's pasted notation (hatching, dimension lines, a footer key).
briefs.title: "Tell Vera our *plans*." Not yet tried. It keeps what made the lineage's title the heat-b favourite: her name, the verb 'tell' that makes the box an invitation to write, and the lit job word at the line's end where the eye stops. It speaks in the family's 'our', and that matches Fig. 0 beside it, the household wired into her screen. The plural answers the skeptic's objection to 'What's the plan?' and 'Tell Vera our plan.' that it presumes one plan already exists. 'Plans' is what the family hands her a piece at a time: a weekend, a reminder, an idea to keep, a wish. It also echoes the placeholder below ('Plans for the weekend, …'), which reads as the answers. At 20 characters, set in Plex Sans Condensed 600 at clamp(2.25rem, 7vw, 3.25rem), it holds one line on a 360px phone. No other glow on Home claims 'plans': the terminal reads '5 plans' at normal strength, not lit. It stays the box's
